Score 40-90% Off Market Value – Wake County, North Carolina Tax Deed Investing

Discover incredible deals on properties at Wake County, North Carolina’s Tax Foreclosure Sales, where you can find homes for up to 90% off market value.

Wake County’s tax foreclosure sales provide an excellent opportunity for real estate investors to acquire properties at significantly reduced prices. Unlike many states, North Carolina does not sell tax lien certificates. Instead, counties like Wake County initiate foreclosure proceedings when property taxes are not paid. Here’s a detailed guide to help you get started:

Understanding the Foreclosure Process

In Wake County, the foreclosure process begins when the Department of Tax Administration dockets a foreclosure judgment with the court system for unpaid property taxes. The judgment is docketed 30 days after the property owner is notified by certified mail or publication. If the delinquent taxes, including interest and costs, are not paid before the judgment is docketed, the property is prepared for public auction.

Steps to Participate in Wake County’s Tax Deed Sales

Research Local Laws: Understanding the legal framework is crucial. Wake County follows specific procedures for tax foreclosures and auctions.

Visit the County’s Websites:

  • Wake County Foreclosures Information
  • Wake County Tax Administration
  • Wake County Main Site

Check the Auction Site: Auctions are conducted by the Sheriff’s Office inside the Salisbury Street entrance of the Wake County Courthouse. Notice of the sale is advertised in The News & Observer and posted on the courthouse bulletin board 20 days prior to the auction.

Prepare for the Auction:

Auctions typically occur about four months after the court dockets a judgment.

You must provide a 10% cash deposit of the winning bid at the auction.

Prepare for upset bids. Successful bids are open for a 10-day period to allow for upset bids, which must be at least 5% higher than the original bid or $750, whichever is greater. Make upset bids with the Clerk of the Superior Court.

Contact the County Office: For further details or questions, you can reach out via email at taxhelp@wake.gov or by phone at 919-856-5400.

Important Details

Why Wake County is a Top Choice for Tax Deed Investors

  • Great Investment Potential
    Wake County has a strong economy and is home to one of North Carolina’s fastest-growing cities, Raleigh. As a result, real estate in the area can see considerable appreciation. This makes tax deed sales in the county a great way to tap into the region’s thriving property market at a steep discount.
  • Accessible Information and Resources
    The Wake County Tax Administration helps you get started by providing comprehensive resources. They include detailed property listings and auction process guidelines.

Pro Tips for Success in Wake County Tax Deed Auctions

  1. Do Your Research
    Before attending an auction, research each property thoroughly. Check for any liens, legal issues, or damages that could affect your investment.
  2. Understand the Rules
    Make sure you understand the upset bid process and the deposit requirements before attending an auction.
  3. Know the Market
    Get a feel for property values in the area so you can gauge whether you’re getting a good deal or not.
  4. Prepare for Upset Bids
    Have a backup plan in case someone outbids you during the upset bid period. You may need to increase your bid or walk away.
